entries.Name: Low Receiving World K-11
entries.Description: the failure caused procedure to split. Acceptance, storage, movement and release became four separately recorded acts. Later Low Concordance institutions treated any system that collapsed those acts into a single “transfer completed” state as ethically primitive.

Setting.form: Habitation beside work routes; narrow durable rooms; empty load cradle in personal space.

Particularisation.habitation: Habitation beside work routes; narrow durable rooms; empty load cradle in personal space.
Particularisation.clothing: heavy pressure cloth, reinforced shoulders, load-distribution harnesses, removable thermal liners. Rank shown by stitching patterns indicating custody authorisations.
Particularisation.maintenance_sustenance: compact nutrient pastes, mineral broths, temperature-regulated rest. Eating socially uncommon during active custody.
Particularisation.transport: slow rail sledges and floor-guided burden carriers; immobilisation preferred over automatic rerouting when authority becomes uncertain.
Particularisation.work_rhythm: measured by custody state, not clock time.

Particularisation.death_custody: the dead are never described as “cleared” merely because physical space has been recovered.
Particularisation.repair_culture: damaged equipment repaired in place whenever possible.
Particularisation.ordinary_phrase: **“Do not make completion out of movement.”**
Particularisation.kinship: Burden Kin — long-term bonds formed by repeatedly accepting difficult custody together. Biological ancestry matters where it exists, but shared burden history can create stronger obligations.
Particularisation.friendship: a close friend is trusted to take over a burden without erasing its history.
Particularisation.intimacy: private intimacy often involves removing work harnesses, identification surfaces and load permissions in another’s presence. Being seen **unassigned** carries vulnerability.
Particularisation.privacy: personal rooms often have a physical “no transfer” state.
Particularisation.education: new custodians shadow low-risk transfers and maintain chain-of-custody records before touching significant burdens.
Particularisation.mourning: an unresolved task may be preserved exactly as left for years.
Particularisation.humour: a catastrophically complicated situation may be called **“slightly over-received.”**
Particularisation.shame: losing track of an accepted burden.
Particularisation.taboo: saying **“nothing is here”** about an unidentified or unrecorded burden.
Particularisation.hospitality: visitors are formally given a place where nothing will be placed in their custody without consent.
Particularisation.social_exclusion: **non-transfer** — nobody trusts the person with anything that matters.
